# Negotiation and Conflict Management



::: {.callout-note}
This chapter is in preparation. It will be built from **Lecture 10 --
Negotiation and Conflict Management** of MGMT-3105 (and its answer deck),
following the same structure as [Chapter 1](01-Sustainability.qmd) and
[Chapter 9](09-Cost-Estimation-and-Budgeting.qmd).
:::

## Learning objectives (planned)

By the end of this chapter you will be able to:

- Explain why conflict is normal on projects and distinguish functional from dysfunctional conflict.
- Apply the Thomas-Kilmann modes (competing, collaborating, compromising, avoiding, accommodating) to a situation.
- Prepare for a negotiation: interests vs. positions, BATNA, ZOPA, reservation and target points.
- Apply principled negotiation (separate people from problem; focus on interests; invent options; use objective criteria).
- Manage conflict with suppliers, functional managers, and team members.
- Recognise cultural and ethical dimensions of negotiation in a global supply chain.

## Topic outline

1. Sources of project conflict across the life cycle.
2. Conflict-handling modes and when each is appropriate.
3. Distributive vs. integrative negotiation.
4. Preparation: BATNA, ZOPA, anchoring.
5. Principled negotiation.
6. Difficult conversations and escalation paths.
7. Running case: negotiating the motor/control-system supply contract for the RC-vehicle project.
